hypothesis: H-NF19-20: conflict between gradients for two targets
scope: One fixed-checkpoint, fit-only, no-update diagnostic of actual per-target gradients on shared GRU parameters. No PCGrad, optimizer, quality evaluation, or full-sequence-gradient claim.
decision_basis: The corrected design pins the existing R01 wide F0 terminal checkpoint and its 211-input raw-plus-causal-event representation, builds canonical inputs over the complete 0:4224 prefix, and preserves saved normalization.

The two predetermined 128-row windows per sequence use legal sequence-local causal prefixes; hidden state is carried forward under fixed weights and detached at each diagnostic boundary. The stated gradient horizon is explicitly truncated to each window.

Per-target weighted-error numerators share the canonical joint WMSE denominator. Weight-mass pooling of per-window gradients therefore reconstructs the gradient of the declared pooled window objective, provided each window uses the same fixed parameters and detached prefix state.

The named shared blocks exclude the target-specific final output rows, while reporting the shared hidden readout separately. The design requires immutable model state and no optimizer or gradient accumulation.

The sample is limited to eight predeclared R3 fit components and existing train sequences; evaluation sequences, outcome-based replacement, significance claims, and broader training-dynamics claims are excluded.
The one-job CPU, memory, time, and no-retry limits are explicit; the operation estimate and numerical-memory allowance are correctly described as estimates rather than measured runtime or RSS.
implementation_gates: Before any array/model read, bind the exact accepted R3 SAMPLE identity, consumed train-file hashes, canonical input/model/loss source hashes, and checkpoint receipt/hash; reject mismatches without fallback.

Keep the exact 16 windows, per-window joint denominator, parameter-name inventory, and pooling rule fixed. Clearly label the aggregate shared-path vector (inp+gru plus shared hidden readout) separately from the primary inp+gru block, and define norm-ratio and first-order cross-effect sign conventions.

Verify with tiny synthetic checks that per-target losses sum to canonical WMSE and that joint-weighted per-window gradient sums equal the pooled-window gradient; verify hidden-prefix reset/carry semantics and unchanged model state/no populated parameter gradients.
Admit at most the declared capped job; a concrete cap or validity failure ends the diagnostic without changing windows, checkpoint, or resources.
interpretation_limits: Results characterize this checkpoint, these dependent windows, and this truncated gradient horizon only.
Cosine conflict or norm imbalance is a mechanism diagnostic, not evidence of harm, a PCGrad benefit, optimizer-time behavior, or a public-score effect.
No data arrays, checkpoint, model, or remote job were accessed for this design review.
